title: Track remaining pi-mono session/tree/data-structure parity gaps
body:
## Context

Psi has ported the pi-style JSONL session format and now has fast C-side active-session range indexes, but it still does not fully match pi-mono's richer session/tree model.

This issue tracks the remaining feature and architecture gaps so they do not get lost after the performance/indexing PR.

## Current psi state

- Active in-memory session is a linear growable C array of messages.
- The performance PR adds per-message token estimates and a parallel prefix-sum array for fast active-session range queries.
- Entries are stamped with `parentId`, and session headers preserve `parentSession`.
- `/fork [N]` and `/clone [path]` write new flat JSONL files.
- Compaction works on the active linear transcript and snaps past leading `tool-result` entries.

## pi-mono structures/features not fully matched

- Full session tree model:
  - `fileEntries[]` containing all typed entries.
  - `byId: Map<string, SessionEntry>` for direct lookup.
  - `leafId` as the active position.
  - Parent traversal from active leaf to root.
  - Sibling branches preserved inside one session file.

- Tree navigation UX:
  - `/tree` interactive navigation.
  - Branch selection and branch switching.
  - Session picker/tree UI parity.

- Branch-aware operations:
  - Branch-aware forks that operate from an arbitrary tree node.
  - Branch-aware compaction and summaries.
  - Branch summaries and labels integrated into traversal.
  - Clone/fork preserving selected active path rather than only flat message prefixes.

- Semantic token accounting:
  - pi estimates tokens by message/content shape: text blocks, thinking blocks, tool arguments, tool results, images, bash output, summaries.
  - psi currently caches a conservative string heuristic over stored `text` plus `data_json`.
  - Need a semantic estimator that stays cheap enough for portable targets, possibly still indexed in C.

- Indexed session metadata:
  - Children index for parent -> child lookup.
  - Entry id -> entry index map.
  - Active-branch index/cache.
  - Optional prefix token indexes per active branch/path.
  - Label and branch summary indexes if/when those features are ported.

## Possible implementation direction

1. Keep the current C linear active-session hot path for provider/runtime speed.
2. Add a higher-level session entry graph/index layer that mirrors pi-mono's `fileEntries`, `byId`, `leafId`, and child lookups.
3. Make the active transcript a resolved view of the selected tree path.
4. Extend token indexing from linear transcript prefixes to path-aware prefix metadata.
5. Port pi-mono's semantic token estimator, then decide whether it lives in Lua or C.
6. Make compaction operate on resolved branch paths and persist compaction entries without destroying tree history.
7. Add `/tree` and session picker UI after the underlying graph/index model is stable.

## Acceptance criteria

- Existing flat `/fork`, `/clone`, `/resume`, and compaction behavior remains compatible.
- A loaded pi-style session with branches can preserve and navigate sibling branches.
- `/tree` can move the active leaf without losing history.
- Compaction records summaries on a branch without rewriting away unrelated branches.
- Context/token accounting remains fast on long sessions.
- Tests cover linear sessions, branched sessions, fork/clone, branch-aware compaction, and semantic token estimates.

title: Add local Nix binary cache for Docker CI
body:
## Background

PR #60 moves Forgejo Actions jobs onto Docker runners. The jobs now run correctly, but each container still pays unnecessary Nix substitution/build setup cost. Forgejo's Actions cache is useful for ordinary workspace paths, but it is not the right mechanism for sharing `/nix/store` paths across isolated job containers.

## Proposal

Add a local Nix binary cache reachable from the Docker runner containers. Harmonia should be the first candidate. `nix-serve` is intentionally not preferred because it is outdated.

Likely shape:

- Run Harmonia on office-desktop.
- Expose it on a container-reachable local address, similar to the current Forgejo loopback proxy approach.
- Configure CI jobs with the local substituter and trusted public key.
- Decide whether CI should only consume from the cache or also publish build outputs to it.
- Document the trust/isolation model for local CI containers.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Docker CI jobs can substitute common Nix paths from the local cache.
- Cache configuration is documented and reproducible.
- No dependency on the GitHub DNS translation workaround.
- `nix-serve` is not used unless Harmonia proves unsuitable.

title: Port pi-mono TUI focus, overlays, and reusable selector/editor components
body:
## Context

The feature audit notes that psi's TUI now has the persistent component/differential-rendering base, but still lacks pi-mono's higher-level interactive surfaces.

Current documented gap from `docs/port-status.md`:

- no focus/overlay stack
- no modal composition layer
- resume/model/theme/thinking/session pickers are still hard-coded paths rather than reusable selector components
- prompt editor and command autocomplete are not component objects

## Desired direction

Keep psi's terminal philosophy: inline TUI, no alt-screen by default, Lua-owned policy/state, C only for terminal primitives.

Implement:

- focusable component contract
- anchored overlay stack
- modal/picker composition primitives
- reusable `SelectList` / `SettingsList` style components
- prompt editor as a component
- command autocomplete as a component

## Acceptance criteria

- Existing TUI behavior remains unchanged unless a picker/modal is open.
- Resume picker can be expressed through the reusable selector path.
- New selectors can be added without hard-coding each loop in `tui_runtime.lua`.
- Keyboard focus, cancel, accept, and redraw behavior are covered by smoke or Lua tests.

Origin: parity gaps documented during PR #144 feature audit.

comments.author: siraben
comments.body:
Audit from `origin/master` at `8ce8980` on branch `siraben/audit-issues`. Master at opening (2026-05-27) was `7ae14bf`.

This is now partly stale. Current master has a real TUI app layer with focus and overlay stack behavior in `lua/psi/tui_app.lua`, plus tests around focus/overlay routing. The remaining gap is the reusable widget/component layer: selectors, editors, modals, pickers, and shared prompt/input components are still mostly bespoke, for example the resume picker in `lua/psi/tui_runtime.lua`.

Verdict: **partially applies; narrow it**. The focus/overlay part should be considered done on master. Keep the issue open only for reusable TUI components and picker/editor surfaces. That direction matches psi if the components stay small Lua modules instead of importing pi-mono's richer UI framework wholesale.

title: Add RPC mode over JSONL stdin/stdout
body:
## Context

`docs/port-status.md` marks pi-mono RPC mode as not started. The audit explicitly left full RPC/SDK mode out of PR #144.

## Scope

Add an RPC mode that reuses the existing runtime/session/provider/tool loop and speaks JSONL over stdin/stdout.

Keep this aligned with psi's architecture:

- C host remains small.
- Lua owns protocol policy and request handling where practical.
- Existing session persistence, provider streaming, abort handling, and tool dispatch are reused.
- No separate backend/server dependency.

## Open design points

- exact wire schema compatibility target with pi-mono
- request lifecycle and streaming event shapes
- how abort/cancel is represented
- how provider/tool errors map into protocol events
- whether this is exposed as `--rpc`, a subcommand, or a mode flag

## Acceptance criteria

- JSONL request/response loop works through stdin/stdout.
- At least one turn can be run with tool calls and streamed assistant output.
- Abort/cancel is protocol-visible and leaves session state coherent.
- Tests cover a happy path, malformed input, provider/tool error, and abort.

Origin: parity gaps documented during PR #144 feature audit.

title: Port skills and package-managed extension workflow
body:
## Context

The audit notes that project context discovery is now closer to pi-mono, but skills are still not ported. `docs/port-status.md` also notes that the extension system is early/partial and has no npm/git package manager, no TS transpile path, and no sandboxing.

This issue tracks the non-sandbox package/skills side. Sandboxing is already separately tracked by #39.

## Desired direction

Design a psi-native skills workflow that stays in philosophy:

- Lua-first and local-file friendly
- no mandatory hosted marketplace
- no heavyweight JS runtime requirement
- clear load order and opt-out behavior
- compatible with existing `PSI_EXTENSIONS_DIR`, global, and project extension loading

## Scope

- skill discovery and loading model
- manifest or metadata format if needed
- install/update workflow for local/git skills
- integration with prompt/resource assembly
- tests for global/project precedence and disable controls

## Acceptance criteria

- A local skill can be installed and loaded predictably.
- Project-local skills can override or augment global skills without surprising global state leaks.
- Users can disable skill loading.
- Docs explain the difference between extensions, prompt templates, and skills.

Origin: parity gaps documented during PR #144 feature audit.

Verdict: **still applies**. This should be scoped to psi's philosophy: local, inspectable Lua/text skills with minimal loader rules. A direct port of pi-mono's package/marketplace assumptions would be too heavy for psi's small-host, Lua-brain design.

title: Stabilize extension provider registration and model catalog parity
body:
## Context

`docs/port-status.md` says provider/model loop is partial-to-ported: built-in Anthropic, Ollama, OpenRouter, and OpenAI Codex share provider routing, but extension-level provider registration and the broad pi model catalog are not ported.

`docs/extensions.md` also says provider registration exists internally but is not yet a stable extension API.

## Scope

- freeze public provider registration/unregistration contracts
- expose a stable extension API for adding providers and models
- decide how provider capabilities are declared and queried
- define model catalog update strategy that does not make psi depend on a broad JS/runtime stack
- keep provider code frontend-agnostic

## Acceptance criteria

- An extension can register a provider and model metadata through documented APIs.
- Registered providers work from `--print`, REPL, and TUI through the same runtime path.
- Runtime capability checks can see extension-provided models.
- Tests cover registration, unregistration/reload cleanup, and provider selection.

Origin: parity gaps documented during PR #144 feature audit.

Current master has internal registry functions in `lua/psi/api_registry.lua`, but `docs/extensions.md` still says provider/model registration is not stable and reload cleanup/unregistration is not part of the extension contract.

Verdict: **still applies**. This is aligned with psi if implemented as a Lua-first extension API with clear lifecycle/reload semantics. It should stay frontend-agnostic and should not become a plugin/package-manager framework modeled directly on pi-mono.

title: Implement full pi-style prompt cache-key controls
body:
## Context

`docs/port-status.md` says system prompt assembly is ported, but prompt-cache controls remain provider-specific rather than a full pi cache-key implementation.

## Scope

- audit pi-mono prompt cache-key semantics
- decide which cache markers/metadata should be represented in psi session records
- make provider cache behavior derive from shared prompt/session metadata instead of provider-specific one-offs
- preserve psi's provider-agnostic runtime loop

## Acceptance criteria

- Cache behavior is described in shared Lua prompt/session code, not only inside individual providers.
- Anthropic/OpenAI-compatible/OpenAI Codex paths consume the shared cache metadata consistently where their APIs support it.
- Session replay does not lose or duplicate cache metadata.
- Tests cover system prompt changes, context file changes, tool metadata changes, and provider differences.

Origin: parity gaps documented during PR #144 feature audit.

comments.author: siraben
comments.body:
Audit from `origin/master` at `8ce8980` on branch `siraben/audit-issues`. Master at opening (2026-05-27) was `7ae14bf`.

At opening, prompt caching was provider-specific. Current master is still provider-specific: Anthropic sets `cache_control` blocks, while OpenAI/Codex mostly parses cached-token usage and does not expose shared controls like pi-mono's session/cache retention/cache-key plumbing.

Verdict: **still applies**. The pi-mono comparison is useful, but the psi-shaped version should be a small Lua-level cache metadata model that providers may consume. Avoid baking pi-mono's full TypeScript runtime abstractions into the C host.

title: Add extension hooks for compaction customization and cancellation
body:
## Context

Compaction itself is ported and PR #144 made it branch-safe for durable session history, but `docs/port-status.md` still identifies missing extension customization/cancel hooks.

## Scope

Add extension-level hooks around compaction without moving compaction policy into C.

Candidate hook points:

- before compaction prompt construction
- custom summary prompt/context injection
- veto/cancel compaction
- after compaction summary is persisted
- diagnostics/events for TUI and extensions

## Acceptance criteria

- Extensions can observe and customize compaction through documented Lua APIs.
- An extension can cancel compaction cleanly before provider work starts.
- A canceled compaction leaves session state unchanged and user-visible status clear.
- Tests cover hook ordering, cancellation, and reload cleanup.

Origin: parity gaps documented during PR #144 feature audit.

comments.author: siraben
comments.body:
Audit from `origin/master` at `8ce8980` on branch `siraben/audit-issues`. Master at opening (2026-05-27) was `7ae14bf`.

At opening, compaction hooks were observe-only. Current master is still that way: extensions see `compaction-start` / `compaction-end`, but there is no before-compact hook that can alter instructions, veto/cancel, or attach compaction-specific metadata before the provider call.

Verdict: **still applies**. Compared with pi-mono's `session_before_compact` hook and custom compact instructions, psi is missing the extension point. This fits psi's philosophy if kept as a small Lua event/decision hook owned by the session layer; it should not pull policy or provider-specific compaction behavior into C.

title: Evaluate an AgentSession-equivalent runtime facade for psi modes
body:
## Context

`docs/port-status.md` marks the central session/runtime object as partial. Psi intentionally has a smaller C observer/runtime bridge plus Lua session/runtime modules, but it does not have a single `AgentSession`-equivalent object that owns every mode like pi-mono.

This may be fine architecturally; the issue is to evaluate whether a Lua facade would reduce drift across `--print`, REPL, TUI, compact, resume, and future RPC without bloating the C host.

## Scope

- audit duplicated mode bootstrap/session/provider setup
- identify mode-specific behavior that should remain separate
- decide whether a Lua `agent_session` facade should own turn lifecycle, resume/bootstrap, compaction, abort wiring, and observer events
- keep C as host boundary only

## Acceptance criteria

- Clear design note deciding whether to add a facade or explicitly keep the current split.
- If implemented, `--print`, REPL, TUI, and compact share the facade for common lifecycle behavior.
- Existing mode-specific UX remains unchanged.
- Tests cover at least one shared lifecycle path across multiple modes.

Origin: parity gaps documented during PR #144 feature audit.

comments.author: siraben
comments.body:
Audit from `origin/master` at `8ce8980` on branch `siraben/audit-issues`. Master at opening (2026-05-27) was `7ae14bf`.

Current master has moved in this direction with `lua/psi/agent_session.lua`, which centralizes provider/model state and turn/side-question/compact entry points. It is not fully the runtime object described here: `lua/psi/modes.lua` still owns much of session bootstrap, resume/save, observer setup, and the REPL loop.

Verdict: **still applies, but as a design/refinement issue rather than a greenfield feature**. The psi-compatible target is a small Lua session/runtime object that reduces mode coupling while keeping C as the host shell. The pi-mono comparison is useful for responsibilities, not for copying its heavier session class structure wholesale.

title: Codex tool-call command arguments truncated by final char (`print`->`prin`, `nproc`->`npro`)
body:
### Summary

While using the `openai-codex` provider, tool-call command arguments have been observed **truncated by their final character** — e.g. `print` rendered/executed as `prin` (`sh: prin\u000f: not found`) and `nproc` becoming `npro`. The trailing `\u000f` (SI control byte) in one report suggests a control-character leak from the tool-execution / PTY layer rather than plain truncation.

### Investigation so far (not yet reproduced)

- `lua/psi/stream_parser.lua` (SSE/line framing) was reviewed: `push_lines` correctly buffers partial lines across chunk boundaries and only dispatches on a real `\n`; `push_sse` handles `data:`/`data: ` prefixes and blank-line dispatch. **No off-by-one or trailing-byte drop found here.**
- `lua/psi/providers/openai_codex.lua` tool-call handling was reviewed: `response.function_call_arguments.delta` appends deltas; `response.function_call_arguments.done` overwrites `arg_text` with the complete `event.arguments`; `function_call` items copy `item.arguments` whole. **No truncation found in the parser.**
- Compared against pi-mono `packages/ai/src/api/openai-responses-shared.ts` — psi mirrors the same accumulate-then-finalize shape.

### Hypotheses to pursue

1. Control-char (`\u000f`) injection in the **tool execution / PTY display** path (`lua/psi/tool_shell.lua` / TUI command echo), truncating on render rather than in the arg value.
2. A model/provider-side streamed-args edge case where the final delta is not flushed before `output_item.done` under a specific event ordering.

### Repro needed

Capture a raw Codex Responses SSE stream that produces the truncated arg, and assert the decoded tool-call argument end-to-end (`tests/lua/providers/openai_codex_parser.lua` is the natural home for a regression case).

_Filed by an overnight maintenance agent; carrying forward an unfinished investigation thread from recent sessions so it is not lost. No code change made because the defect is not yet reproducible._
